## Introduction

We will generate linear models using the `brms` package. Posterior draws will be extracted using `tidybayes` and the probability (i.e., percentage value ranging from 0% to 100%) that an estimate is in favour of a given protocol will be calculated manually by examining the proportion of posterior draws that meets the criteria of interest (e.g., >0 or >TE)  For normally distributed data, Bayesian linear models will be generated to assess mean differences between protocols, with the pre-intervention or first set value assigned as a covariate for models assessing change in muscle thickness from pre-to post-intervention.

## Load libraries

First we load the libraries we need and set up our working environment.

```{r}
#| label: Set up environment

library(tidyverse) # Data wrangling, plotting
library(brms) # Bayesian estimation
library(tidybayes) # 'Tidy' results
library(bayesplot) # Convenient plotting
library(ggridges) # For forest plot
library(readxl) # To read data files
library(rstan) # Bayesian modelling
library(ggplot2) # For plots
library(posterior)# Posterior distributions
library(glue) # For plots
library(ggpubr) # For Plots
library (bayestestR) # For probability of direction
library(emmeans) # For contrasts
library(rstatix) # Assess normality
library(gt) # Tables
library(dplyr) # Data frames
library(ggh4x) # For plots
library(datawizard) # Data wrangling
library(patchwork) # For plots
library(lme4) # Traditional modelling
library(performance) # Model quality

```

## Muscle hypertrophy

To assess differences in muscle hypertrophy between the FAIL and RIR protocols, a linear model will be generated with the following response variable: 

  1) Change in Muscle Thickness (from pre- to post-intervention)
  
One additional interaction factor will be added into the model:

  1) Muscle measured (RF or VL)

This model will account for baseline differences in muscle size and differences between the muscles measured, which is important, especially considering we have a sample of males and females and specific muscles may respond differently to exercises. Group level slope structure for each participant will involve 'protocol' and each limb will be nested within each participant.

### Generate model

We will use `brms` to run the primary linear model to generate Bayesian estimates of the change in muscle thickness (from pre- to post-intervention) for FAIL and RIR protocols and the complete posterior distributions.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian linear modelling

model.matrix(muscle.thickness ~ protocol * muscle + Pre, data = rf_vl_master) # Assess model matrix

# Generate model
MT_model <- brm(muscle.thickness ~ protocol * muscle + Pre + (protocol|id) + (1|id:limb),
                data = rf_vl_master,
                seed = 123,
                control = list(adapt_delta=0.99))
summary(MT_model)
                
#plot(MT_model) # Preliminary diagnostics

```

Calculate Bayesian estimates generated from the linear model.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian estimates from linear model

# By protocol only
MT_effects <- emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol, weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(MT_effects, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
MT_effects_contrast <- pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol, weights = "prop"))
  hpd.summary(MT_effects_contrast, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
MT_effects_GG <- emmeans(MT_model, spec = ~protocol, weights = "prop") %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

MT_effects_contrast_GG <- pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol, weights = "prop")) %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

# By protocol and muscle and contrast for each muscle
MT_effects_muscle <- emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol|muscle, weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(MT_effects_muscle, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
MT_effects_contrast_muscle <- pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol|muscle, weights = "prop"))
  hpd.summary(MT_effects_contrast_muscle, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
MT_effects_GG_muscle <- emmeans(MT_model, spec = ~protocol|muscle, weights = "prop") %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

MT_effects_GG_contrast_muscle <- pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol|muscle, weights = "prop")) %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

```

### Model interpretation

To interpret the results in the most complete manner, we will construct a ggplot of the posterior distributions for each protocol and each muscle, along with the contrast for each muscle.

1) By protocol (averaged over RF and VL)

```{r}
#| label: Construct ggplot

ggplot(MT_effects_GG, aes(x = .value, y = protocol, fill = protocol)) + 
     geom_rect(data=NULL,aes(xmin=te_avg,xmax=1,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf),
                    fill="#F5F5F5") +
    geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0 + te_avg,
    colour = 'grey',
    linetype = 'dashed',
    linewidth = .8) + 
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    colour = 'black',
    linetype = 'dashed',
    linewidth = .8) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = 0.95, point_interval = mean_hdi) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E74C3C", "#3498DB")) +
  stat_slabinterval(
    slab_color = "black",
    slab_linetype = 1,
    slab_size = 1,
    point_size = 4.5
  ) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0),
                     breaks = c(-0.1, 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.12, 0.37), ylim = c(1.2,2.5)) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.line = element_line(size = .8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = .8, colour = "black"),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(
      family = "Helvetica",
      size = 12,
      colour = "black"
    )
  )
    
```

We will now calculate the probability (i.e., percentage value ranging from 0% to 100%) that an estimate is in favour of a given protocol by examining the proportion of posterior draws that met the criteria of interest (e.g., either >0 or >TE)

```{r}
#| label: Calculate results for manuscript reporting

# By protocol
emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol, weights = "prop")%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
group_by(protocol)%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# By protocol over TE
emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol, weights = "prop")%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
group_by(protocol)%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>te_avg,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# By protocol and muscle over TE for RF
emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol|muscle, weights = "prop")%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>rf_te_avg,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# By protocol and muscle over TE for VL
emmeans(MT_model, ~ protocol|muscle, weights = "prop")%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>vl_te_avg,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol (>o)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
group_by(contrast)%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol (>TE)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
group_by(contrast)%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>te_avg,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol by RF (<0)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol|muscle, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value<0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol by VL (>0)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol|muscle, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol by RF (<TE)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol|muscle, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value<(-rf_te_avg),na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for protocol by VL (>TE)
pairs(emmeans(MT_model, ~protocol|muscle, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value>vl_te_avg,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

```


## Lifting Velocity

To assess differences in loss of lifting velocity between the FAIL and RIR protocols, a linear model will be generated with the following response variable:

  1) Change in lifting velocity (first to final set) calculated as a percentage value
  
One additional interaction factors will be added into the model:

  1) Time point (WEEK 1, WEEK 4, WEEK 8)

This model will account for the absolute lifting velocity of the first set (as this value could influence the percentage change), total number of sets performed, and participant sex, and will allow us to investigate an interaction effect, which is important, as measurements of lifting velocity were taken at WEEKS 1, 4 and 8. Group level slope structure for each participant will involve 'protocol * time + first_set + sets' and each limb will be nested within each participant.

### Generate model

We will use `brms` to run the primary linear model to generate Bayesian estimates of the change in lifting velocity (first to final set) for FAIL and RIR protocols.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian linear modelling

model.matrix(lifting_velocity ~ 1 + protocol * time + first_set + sets, data = vl_master) # Assess model matrix

LV_model <- brm(percent_diff ~ protocol * time + sex + first_set + sets + (protocol * time + first_set + sets|id) + (1|id:limb),
                data = vl_master,
                seed = 123,
                control = list(adapt_delta=0.99))
summary(LV_model)

#plot(LV_model) # Preliminary diagnostics

```

Calculate Bayesian estimates (and contrast estimates) generated from the linear model.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian estimates from linear model

# Means for protocol and time
LV_effects <- emmeans(LV_model, ~ protocol*time, point.est = mean)
  hpd.summary(LV_effects, point.est = mean) # Display mean

LV_effects_full <- pairs(emmeans(LV_model, ~ time*protocol, point.est = mean))

# Contrasts for protocol and time
LV_effects_contrasts <- emmeans(LV_model, ~protocol * time)
  hpd.summary(LV_effects_contrasts, point.est = mean) # Display mean

LV_effects_time <- pairs(LV_effects_contrasts, by = "time") 
  hpd.summary(LV_effects_time, point.est = mean) # Display mean

LV_effects_protocol <- pairs(LV_effects_contrasts, by = "protocol")
  
LV_effects_time_GG <- pairs(LV_effects_contrasts, by = "time") %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

```

### Model interpretation

To interpret the results in the most complete manner, we will construct a ggplot to display posterior distributions for the contrast between FAIL and RIR for each time point. The values generated represent the difference between FAIL and RIR. Negative values represent greater decreases in lifting velocity for FAIL versus RIR.

```{r}
#| label: Construct ggplot

ggplot(LV_effects_time_GG, aes(x = .value, y = factor(time, level=c('WEEK 8', 'WEEK 4', 'WEEK 1')), fill = stat(x < 0))) + 
  stat_halfeye(.width = 0.95, point_interval = mean_hdi) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E74C3C", "#3498DB")) +
  stat_slabinterval(
    slab_color = "black",
    slab_linetype = 1,
    slab_size = 1,
    point_size = 4.5
  ) + geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    colour = 'black',
    linetype = 'dashed',
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),expand = c(0, 0),
                     breaks = c(-0.15, -0.1,-0.05, 0, 0.05,0.1,0.15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.2, 0.20)) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.line = element_line(size = .8, colour = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = .8, colour = "black"),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(
      family = "Helvetica",
      size = 12,
      colour = "black"
    )
  )

```

We will now calculate the probability (i.e., percentage value ranging from 0% to 100%) that an estimate is in favour of a given protocol by examining the proportion of posterior draws that met the criteria of interest (e.g., >0)

```{r}
#| label: Calculate results for manuscript reporting

# By protocol and time
emmeans(LV_model, ~ protocol*time, weights = "prop")%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value<0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

# Contrast for time
pairs(emmeans(LV_model, ~protocol*time, weights = "prop"))%>%
gather_emmeans_draws()%>%
group_by(contrast)%>%
summarise(pd=round(mean(.value<0,na.rm=TRUE)*100,0))

```

## Repetition Loss

To assess differences in repetition loss between the FAIL and RIR protocols, a linear model will be generated witht the following response variable:

  1) Repetition loss (first to final set) calculated as a percentage value
  
Two additional interaction factors will be added into the model:

  1) Time point (Session, Week)
  2) Exercise (Leg Press, Leg Extension)
  
This model will account for the number of repetitions performed on the first set (as this value could influence the percentage change), total number of sets performed, and participant sex, and will allow us to investigate an interaction effect, which is important, as repetition loss may change overtime and differ between exercises and sexes. Group level slope structure for each participant will involve 'protocol * time * exercise + reps.first + sets' and each limb will be nested within each participant.

### Generate model

We will use `brms` to run the primary linear model to generate Bayesian estimates of repetition loss (first to final set) for FAIL and RIR protocols.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian linear modelling

model.matrix(rep.loss ~ protocol * time * exercise + sex, data = rep_loss_master) # Assess model matrix

# Generate model
RL_model <- brm(rep.loss ~ protocol * time * exercise + sex + reps.first + sets + (protocol * time * exercise + reps.first + sets|id) + (time + exercise + reps.first|id:limb),
            data=rep_loss_master,
            seed=123,
            control = list(adapt_delta=0.99))
summary(RL_model)

#plot(RL_model) # Preliminary diagnostics

```

Calculate Bayesian estimates (and contrast estimates) generated from the linear model.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian estimates from linear model

# Means for protocol, time and exercise
## Time + Protocol + Exercise
RL_effects <- emmeans(RL_model, ~time+protocol+exercise, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop")
    hpd.summary(RL_effects, point.est = mean) 
RL_effects_GG <- emmeans(RL_model, ~time+protocol+exercise, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop") %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

## Protocol + Exercise
```

## Volume Load

To assess differences in volume load between the FAIL and RIR protocols, a linear model will be generated with the following response variable:

  1) Absolute volume load
  
Two additional interaction factors will be added into the model:

  1) Time point (Session, Week)
  2) Exercise (Leg Press, Leg Extension)

This model will account for total number of sets performed and participant sex, and will allow us to investigate an interaction effect, which is important, as volume load may change overtime and differ between exercises and sexes. Group level slope structure for each participant will involve 'protocol * time * exercise + sets' and each limb will be nested within each participant.

### Generate model

We will use `brms` to run the primary linear model to generate Bayesian estimates of the volume load completed for FAIL and RIR protocols.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian linear modelling

model.matrix(volume.load ~ protocol * time * exercise + sex, data = volume_master) # Assess model matrix

# Generate model
VL_model <- brm(volume.load ~ protocol * time * exercise + sex + sets + (protocol * time * exercise + sets|id) + (1|id:limb),
                data = volume_master,
                seed = 123,
                control = list(adapt_delta=0.99, max_treedepth = 12))
summary(VL_model)

#plot(VL_model) # Preliminary diagnostics

```

Calculate Bayesian estimates (and contrast estimates) generated from the linear model.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian estimates from linear model

# Means for protocol, time and exercise
## Time + Protocol + Exercise
VL_effects <- emmeans(VL_model, ~time+protocol+exercise, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(VL_effects, point.est = mean)
VL_effects_GG <- emmeans(VL_model, ~time+protocol+exercise, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop") %>% gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

## Protocol + Exercise
VL_effects_protocol <- emmeans(VL_model, ~protocol+exercise, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(VL_effects_protocol, point.est = mean)

## Protocol + Time
VL_effects_time <- emmeans(VL_model, ~protocol+time, at=list(time=1:16), weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(VL_effects_time, point.est = mean) 

# Means and contrasts of slopes
VL_trends=emtrends(VL_model,
         var = "time",
         pairwise~protocol|exercise)

## Mean of slopes for each exercise
hpd.summary(VL_trends$emtrends, point.est = mean)
VL_trends_GG=VL_trends$emtrends%>%
  gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

## Contrast of slopes for each exercise
hpd.summary(VL_trends$contrasts, point.est = mean)
VL_contrasts_GG=VL_trends$contrasts%>%
  gather_emmeans_draws() # For ggplot

```
